question.text: Optical activity of an enantiomeric mixture is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and the specific rotation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mo>+</mo></mfenced></math> isomer is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. The optical purity is____<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math>

solution.text:
The "optical purity" is a comparison of the optical rotation of a pure sample of unknown stereochemistry versus the optical rotation of a sample of pure enantiomer. It is expressed as a percentage. If the sample only rotates plane-polarized light half as much as expected, the optical purity is 50%.

% optical purity =observed rotation of mixture×100rotation of pure enantiomer

=+12.6°+30°×100=42
